plan.title: bug(scope-provenance): verify:scope-provenance runs past 5 minutes with no output in a fresh worktree

narratives.Description: `verify:scope-provenance` takes about five minutes in this repository and prints nothing while it runs, because the lifecycle census starts one `git show` process for each of about 1,980 briefs at the base ref. This story reads the census through a few size-budgeted `git cat-file` batches with today's single read as the fallback, keeps the texts for the rest of the run, writes one stderr line per phase, and gives every git call of the check a per-call time limit (120 seconds by default) that ships in warn mode. The verdict, the findings and the exit codes stay the same.
narratives.UserStory: As a worker or CI job running `verify:scope-provenance`, I want the check to finish in seconds and name the phase it is in, so that a run no longer looks hung and a truly blocked git call is named and bounded.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: One product PR (deft-story: 6378). 1. New `packages/core/src/scope-provenance/git-call.ts`: one git runner for the check (spawnSync with `timeout` and `killSignal: "SIGKILL"`, env `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`, the 64 MiB buffer), the declared refusal row `scope-provenance-git-call-timeout` (mode `warn`, remedy), the timeout error kind, the warn line and the retry with no limit, and the resolution flag > `DEFT_SCOPE_PROVENANCE_GIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` > 120. 2. New `packages/core/src/scope-provenance/census-batch.ts`: the lifecycle census moved out of evaluate.ts with the same listing, path rules and errors, plus the batched reader (partition, one `--batch-check`, budgeted `--batch` chunks parsed as bytes, whole fallback on any mismatch). 3. `evaluate.ts`: route every git call through the runner, keep census texts in one in-run map served by the base reader, phase callbacks, a timeout in enforce mode returns exit 2 with the line. 4. Runtime `verify-scope-provenance.ts`: `--git-timeout-seconds`, phase lines with `fs.writeSync(2, ...)` unless `--quiet`, the remedy line. 5. Tests per acceptance line, docs section, changelog fragment, before/after timings in the PR body.
narratives.Overview:
1. Same listing, same paths, same ref. The census keeps its `git ls-tree --name-only` listing per lifecycle folder at the selected base ref, and keeps today's path decoding, trimming, normalising and lifecycle filter. It makes one read request per listed entry, in listing order, for `<ref>:<normalised path>`, the string that `git show` receives today. Two entries that normalise to the same path stay two requests and two census entries.
2. Partition before any batch call. A request is batch-eligible only when its path is printable ASCII with no control character. Every other request is read with today's single `git show` and is never sent to a batch call.
3. Sizes of the eligible requests. One `git cat-file --batch-check` call takes the eligible request strings. A request whose record is not a `blob` (for example `missing`, `tree` or `commit`) is read with today's single `git show`.
4. Budgeted batches. The remaining requests go to `git cat-file --batch` in chunks. A chunk's budget counts, for each record, its content size plus the header line and the trailing delimiter, and the sum stays under the existing subprocess buffer limit. The output is parsed as bytes by each record's header size, and each object is decoded as UTF-8 by itself. A request whose own framed answer does not fit is read with today's single `git show`.
5. Batch is an accelerator only. If a batch call exits non-zero, or its records do not match the requests one for one in order with the id and size from item 3, the census discards the batch results and reads every entry with today's single reads. The census errors, the missing-versus-error distinction and the JSON handling are produced only by today's code.
6. One in-run text map. Texts read by the census are kept for that one evaluate, keyed by ref and normalised path. The base reader serves from the map and falls back to today's single read for any other path. Injected readers keep their precedence. Nothing is cached between runs.
7. Phase lines. Before base resolution, the change-set read, the census (with its brief count) and the per-story evaluation, the runtime writes one line that names the phase to file descriptor 2 with a synchronous write (`fs.writeSync`). `--quiet` suppresses the lines. Stdout, the verdict and the exit code do not change.
8. Per-call time limit, on by default. Every git call of this check is started with the `timeout` option of `spawnSync` and `killSignal: "SIGKILL"`. At the limit the operating system ends the git process; git cannot handle or ignore that signal, and on Windows Node ends the process unconditionally. `spawnSync` returns when that process has exited, and only then does the check act on the result. The default is 120 seconds per call. The flag `--git-timeout-seconds <n>` on the verb overrides it, and `0` means no limit. The environment variable `DEFT_SCOPE_PROVENANCE_GIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` overrides the default for runs that cannot pass the flag; the flag wins over the variable. A call that reaches the limit is its own error kind: it is not folded into the census read failure and it does not trigger the item 5 fallback.
9. No optional locks. Every git call of this check runs with `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`, so a call that is ended at the limit does not leave an index lock behind.
10. Warn first, then refuse. The limit is one declared refusal with the id `scope-provenance-git-call-timeout`, a mode and a remedy, in the form of the #6281 declaration table (lean 6908087379 on #6281). It ships in `warn` mode. In `warn` mode, after `spawnSync` has returned from the ended call, one line names the id, the phase, the git command, the elapsed seconds and the remedy and says the check can refuse from a later release; the same command is then run once more with no limit. In `enforce` mode the same line is the refusal and the check exits 2. The change to `enforce` is a later one-line change with its own CHANGELOG entry. The remedy is the verb with a larger `--git-timeout-seconds` value. If the #6281 table and helper exist when this is built, the row and the line use them. If they do not, the row is a constant in the scope-provenance module with the same fields and the same line, and it moves to the table when the table exists.

The code supports the diagnosis: the census starts a separate Git process for every lifecycle brief. Batching can remove that cost, but “one batched read” alone does not establish equivalent behavior. A straightforward replacement can introduce size-related refusals, read different paths, or change failure handling. The approach remains viable with those compatibility boundaries made explicit.

### 1. blocks-the-design — A batch-wide buffer limit changes accepted inputs

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate.ts:180–205,430–485` applies `SUBPROCESS_MAX_BUFFER` separately to each `git show`. `packages/core/src/subprocess/max-buffer.ts:17` sets it to 64 MiB.

**Failure mode:** Many individually valid briefs can exceed 64 MiB collectively. Capturing the batch through the existing helper would fail where individual reads succeed. Raising the aggregate limit alone also changes behavior by potentially accepting a single oversized brief previously refused.

**Disposition:** The mechanism needs bounded, byte-framed consumption with the existing per-object size behavior preserved. Payload boundaries must be determined before UTF-8 decoding; decoded string lengths cannot safely delimit byte-sized records. A single aggregate capture with the existing limit cannot satisfy the equivalence claim.

### 2. blocks-the-design — Path and failure semantics require an explicit compatibility adapter

**Evidence:** `evaluate.ts:249–283,301–314,446–480` decodes quoted paths, trims and normalizes them, filters them, then reads the resulting path. Missing reads, other read failures, and malformed JSON have distinct handling. `continuity.ts:15–21` supplies the lifecycle filter.

**Failure mode:** An object-ID implementation can read the object originally listed rather than the normalized path the current implementation reads. For example, a filename ending in a space can be trimmed into an eligible `.xbrief.json` path; today the subsequent lookup targets the trimmed name. Reading the original object ID instead changes that result. Conversely, feeding decoded filenames containing newlines into a line-delimited batch request changes request boundaries.

A successful batch process also cannot, by itself, establish that every requested object was returned completely. Treating absent or truncated records as an empty census would lose the existing refusal.

**Disposition:** Preserve the current selection and lookup semantics, request-to-result association, missing/error distinction, and complete-census requirement. Safe framing or object-ID requests can address transport ambiguity, but adopting corrected pathname semantics is a separate behavior change. Existing injected readers at `evaluate.ts:837–858` also need to retain their precedence.

### 3. sharpens-framing — The “merge-base census” actually reads the selected base ref

**Evidence:** `evaluate.ts:760–763` assigns the selected ref directly to `discoveryBaseRef`; `837–881` uses that ref for census listing and reads. By contrast, `990–1000` explicitly computes `git merge-base` for the policy read.

**Failure mode:** Implementing the proposal literally against the actual merge-base commit changes census contents when the base branch has advanced. Lifecycle identities and continuity decisions can consequently differ.

1. Same listing, same paths, same ref. 2. Partition before any batch call. A request is batch-eligible only when its path is printable ASCII with no control character. Every other request is read with today's single `git show` and is never sent to a batch call.
3. Sizes of the eligible requests. One `git cat-file --batch-check` call takes the eligible request strings. A request whose record is not a `blob` (for example `missing`, `tree` or `commit`) is read with today's single `git show`.
4. Budgeted batches. The remaining requests go to `git cat-file --batch` in chunks. A chunk's budget counts, for each record, its content size plus the header line and the trailing delimiter, and the sum stays under the existing subprocess buffer limit. The output is parsed as bytes by each record's header size, and each object is decoded as UTF-8 by itself. A request whose own framed answer does not fit is read with today's single `git show`.
5. Batch is an accelerator only. If a batch call exits non-zero, or its records do not match the requests one for one in order with the id and size from item 3, the census discards the batch results and reads every entry with today's single reads. 4. Budgeted batches. The remaining requests go to `git cat-file --batch` in chunks. ## Summary

`task verify:scope-provenance` ran for more than five minutes in a fresh worktree and printed no result. The cause is not known. Split out of #6336 (pain P11) by operator decision on 2026-11-16.

## What we saw

- Wave 2a (2026-11-15/16): a parent run of `task verify:scope-provenance` on a freshly created story worktree was stopped by a timeout after five minutes with no output.

- The design arc on #6336 found that a progress line alone does not fix the delay, and that a timer cannot fire while a synchronous git call is blocked (audit comment 6907467218 on #6336).

## Expected

First a diagnosis: where the time goes in a fresh worktree. Then a fix for that cause. The check keeps its verdict and its exit codes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a fresh worktree of this repository, when `task verify:scope-provenance` runs, then this issue records the measured time of each step (engine start, dependency resolution, each git call).
- Given a fresh worktree after the fix, when `task verify:scope-provenance` runs, then it prints its result in under 60 seconds.
- Given a git call or a start-up step that runs longer than 30 seconds, then the task prints one line that names the step it is in.
- Given the same change set, then the verdict and the exit code are the same as before the fix.
